resolutions: Optative is a mood for wishes and hopes; command and exhortation are sentence uses of that mood, not a separate imperative mood.
Nonpast and past optatives use their own optative formation, while future and preterit optatives borrow indicative forms and are identified by sentence use.
A preterit optative requires antecessive ō even though the same preterit form can occur without optative use.
First- and third-person commands require mā or tlā because the VNC form alone may not distinguish optative use; second-person x or xi permits omission.
Direct command, indirect command, and exhortation are derived from second-, third-, and first-person subjects respectively.
Mā and tlā stay outside the VNC formula while x or xi, person, number, stem, tense, and object material stay inside it.
Negative wishes and introduced negative commands change ah to prefixal ca; a blunt second-person command without mā keeps ah.
The separate ahmō alternative expresses a negative command without being combined with the ah or ca negative transformation.
A future command uses the future indicative shape with command force supplied by its sentence context; quin may specify later.
Lesson 9 reuses Mood, Tense, Subject, sentence purpose, Polarity, and Particles; automatic form choice and placement do not become extra user controls.
